source: 1968 Chevrolet Chassis Service Manual, Rear Suspension and Drive Line, p.4-33

procedures.title: Axle drive shaft: remove, repair and install
steps: (continued) Repairs: remove the bearing lock ring from the trunnion yoke.
Set the yoke on a length of 1-1/4" pipe on an arbor press bed.
Press the trunnion down with a socket or rod until the opposite bearing cup is pushed out of the yoke.
Take out the trunnion and press out the other cup, without dropping the cup or losing rollers.
Do the other joint the same way.
Take the dust seals off the trunnion; clean and inspect the rollers and trunnion; repack the bearings with high-melting-point wheel bearing grease.
Fit new dust seals with the seal cavity toward the trunnion end; put J-21556 over the trunnion end into the seal cavity and press until the tool bottoms on the trunnion (see figure 83 in the manual).
Start one cup into the yoke, set the trunnion into it, add the other cup, and press both cups in while keeping the trunnion aligned.
Press the cups in far enough to fit the lock rings, and fit them.
Installation: set the inboard trunnion into the side gear yoke and fit the U-bolts; turn the yokes so the trunnion seats are 90 degrees apart.
Fit the outboard flange into the spindle drive flange pilot, lay the bolt lock over the holes and fit the 4 bolts; torque to specification and bend the lock tabs flat against the bolt heads.
notes: Besides packing the bearings, fill the grease reservoir at the end of each trunnion completely, packing from the bottom of the hole to avoid air pockets.
Seal fitting is critical: use the specified tool so the seal does not distort and seats properly.
A bench vise can be used instead of an arbor press, following the same steps.

procedures.title: Pinion flange, dust deflector and/or oil seal: replace
steps: Removal: raise the car and put a stand under the frame so the wheels hang free.
Put a 1/2" wood or steel block between the top of the carrier behind the companion flange and the body floor, so the carrier cannot twist up when the front bracket is freed.
Unbolt the carrier front mounting bracket from the frame crossmember.
Remove the nuts and the 2 bracket-to-carrier through bolts, and take off the bracket.
Disconnect the propeller shaft at the transmission and at the companion flange; slide the transmission yoke forward and lower the shaft out.
Mark the flange nut position relative to the pinion so the original pinion bearing preload can be reset.
Hold the flange with J-8614-1 and remove the nut and washer (see figure 84 in the manual).
Drive the flange off with a brass drift and hammer (see figure 85 in the manual).
Pry the oil seal out of the carrier with a screwdriver.
Inspection: check the flange splines for heavy wear or twisting and the deflector for looseness; if loose or damaged, break the stakes, remove it, fit a new one and stake it.
Installation: pack the space between the seal lips with lithium-base extreme pressure grease...
